speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned waking up frightened; does this happen every night or just occasionally, and do you snore loudly during sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terrors (Sleep Terror Disorder)

The patient is an 8-year-old experiencing episodes of waking up frightened, yelling, and crying once or twice a week, with no confusion afterward and an appearance of tiredness the next day. These features are characteristic of night terrors, which typically occur during non-REM sleep and are distinct from nightmares where the child is usually awake and able to recall the dream.
